title: Rahm edges ahead of Hatton & McIlroy in Abu Dhabi
article_text:
Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention.

The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.

Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under.

Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy remains in hot pursuit, however, after bouncing back in spectacular fashion since being given a two-shot penalty in the opening round for improving his lie before taking a chip shot.

The six-time major winner hit 11 birdies in a second-round 63 and another eight in his third round, but a double bogey six at the par-four 10th - and another dropped shot at the 17th - left McIlroy two shots off the lead.

And he acknowledges that it will take something special on the final day to reel in Rahm and co.

"There are low ones [scores] out there and I am going to have to shoot a low one - something in the mid to low 60s - to get it done tomorrow and that will be the goal," said McIlroy.

Hatton, meanwhile, is looking forward to going head-to-head again with Rahm after playing alongside the two-time major champion, and Laporta, in Saturday's final group.

All three will play together once again on Sunday.

"Obviously final group tomorrow there's a lot to play for," said Hatton, who briefly moved level with Rahm at the top of the leaderboard in the third round after holing his seventh birdie of the day on the 14th.

"Naturally we are going to want to beat each other. Hopefully I can get off to a good start and put him under some pressure."

Rahm, who is chasing his first win in the Abu Dhabi Championship, responded well after being put under pressure by Hatton on Saturday.

He reclaimed the outright lead on the 15th with a superb, curling 20-foot birdie putt and came close to extending his advantage at the last, just coming up short with another birdie chance as he finished without a single dropped shot.

Laporta also produced a bogey-free round to keep pace with the field's big hitters as the 36-year-old, who shot 10 under par to claim a first-round lead, bids for a first title on the DP World Tour.

Elsewhere, Australian Adam Scott remained bogey-free for the tournament after three rounds and moved up to fifth place on 15 under with a 66.

And Englishman Matthew Jordan is a shot further back, alongside Spain's David Puig, after a third-round 69.

title: Jon Rahm makes PGA Tour return harder to ignore, takes Abu Dhabi lead over Rory McIlroy
Bryson DeChambeau set to make major decision with tour future in doubt
article_text:
What next for Bryson DeChambeau after LIV Golf’s collapse? Well, there is surely only one option left…

We will soon know if Bryson DeChambeau intends to play tour golf next year.

The two times major champion is in career limbo after the death knell was sounded LIV Golf, only a week after a podcast was published in which DeChambeau raised hopes that the league would survive forever.

It does not look like there will be an immediate pathway back to the PGA Tour, with chief executive Brian Rolapp adamant he will not make the same offer to LIV players that helped Brooks Koepka return in January.

DeChambeau has long teased the idea of being a solely ‘YouTube golfer’ while competing in the majors, an almost inconceivable idea that has been made possible by his US Open win in 2024, which has secured eligibility in the tournaments that matter most for another three years at least.

But if DeChambeau does wish to play on tour next season, which would surely prove beneficial if he is serious about adding to his major tally while in the peak of his powers, then the DP World Tour is the only attractive landing ground.

DeChambeau will return to the circuit for the $6million Nedbank Challenge next month after accepting an invite from tournament host Gary Player.

But TG understands that DeChambeau’s representatives have been in talks with Wentworth officials about making the DP World Tour more of a full time arrangement.

The Californian has discovered that he would be able to take up a membership category if he so chooses in 2027, owing to an exemption from his victory over Rory McIlroy at Pinehurst two years ago.

The DP World Tour is going to house a swathe of LIV players next season and the prospect of DeChambeau – and the audience he brings – is a tantalising prospect for the money men on a circuit that has become heavily reliant on the PGA Tour.

But DeChambeau will soon need to decide if a season in Europe will satisfy his complex interests.

A deadline of November 16, just after the conclusion of the DP World Tour Championship, has been set for DeChambeau and other eligible players to apply for 2027 membership.

title: Formula 1 Expects Apple to Pursue Broadcast Rights Beyond the U.S. - AppleMagazine
article_text:
Formula 1 expects Apple to pursue broadcasting rights in additional countries when opportunities become available, according to comments from the sport’s leadership. The remarks signal interest in extending the relationship beyond the United States, but do not announce another agreement or identify a market where Apple will launch coverage.

The discussion comes during the first season of Apple’s exclusive American partnership, which has included expanded viewing features for the United States Grand Prix. Any international expansion would require separate rights arrangements rather than automatically extending the U.S. service worldwide.

Speaking during Liberty Media’s third-quarter earnings discussion, Formula 1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali said he expected Apple to participate when opportunities opened elsewhere, according to The Race’s report of the November 5 call.

His comments also preserved an important qualification: Formula 1 is not seeking a single broadcasting partner for the entire world. Its approach remains focused on choosing arrangements market by market.

That distinction leaves several possible outcomes. Apple could bid for rights in selected territories, compete without winning, or decide that particular packages do not fit its plans. An expectation of participation is therefore different from a completed purchase.

Liberty Media president and CEO Derek Chang also described Apple as a potentially helpful bidder, including in markets where another company ultimately wins. His comments identify a commercial benefit for the rights holder: additional competition can strengthen demand for the available packages.

Apple’s five-year Formula 1 agreement began with the 2026 season. It makes Apple the sport’s exclusive U.S. broadcast partner, with coverage of practice, qualifying, Sprint sessions and Grands Prix.

The arrangement includes F1 TV Premium access for U.S. Apple TV subscribers. Apple also committed to promoting the championship through services including Apple News, Maps, Music and Fitness+, with race information available through Apple Sports.

That broader distribution offers a rationale for the partnership beyond the race broadcast itself. A viewer might encounter a circuit guide, a race notification or an editorial feature before deciding to watch a session.

However, the existence of those services internationally does not establish equivalent live-race rights. Apple TV’s availability in a country and its permission to show Formula 1 there are separate matters.

Formula 1’s rights are divided among broadcasters and territories, with agreements running on different schedules. That makes expansion a negotiation process rather than a single global switch.

One current example appears in Liberty Media’s third-quarter results materials, which identify an extended DAZN broadcast agreement covering Spain, Portugal and Andorra through 2030.

An established contract can limit when a competing service has an opportunity to acquire the relevant rights. It can also mean that neighboring countries follow different broadcasting arrangements despite sharing access to the same streaming applications.

For viewers, this explains why an announcement about Apple’s ambitions should not be read as an immediate change to an existing subscription. The relevant evidence would be a named territory, an agreed package and a confirmed starting season.

Acquiring rights establishes permission to distribute coverage, but the viewing experience also depends on the package offered locally. Pricing, commentary languages, supported features and access to supplementary programming would need to be explained for each new arrangement.

The American agreement supplies one model, not a guarantee that every future country would receive identical terms. Rights negotiations can produce different combinations of exclusive coverage, shared distribution or selected events.

Nor do the latest executive comments independently establish the audience performance of Apple’s U.S. coverage. Expectations about future deals and measurements of current viewing are different questions, requiring different evidence.

For U.S. subscribers, the comments do not announce a change to the existing agreement. For audiences elsewhere, they make Apple a company to watch when local rights become available, while leaving current broadcasters and access arrangements in place.

The next meaningful development would be a formal announcement naming a country and a start date. Until then, Formula 1’s leadership has expressed confidence that Apple will consider a broader role, while making clear that the sport intends to keep negotiating its broadcasting business one market at a time.

title: Springboks thrash depleted Italy 66-7 with 9 tries in Nations Championship rugby
England v Australia: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise us - George
article_text:
England hooker Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a newspaper article claiming the end of their summer tour was marked by player unrest over head coach Steve Borthwick's leadership.

A report in the Times, external says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July.

It alleges there are disagreements among Borthwick's wider coaching group, which has been subject to frequent change in his nearly four years in charge, and concerns over the head coach's man-management skills.

England meet Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, with George querying the timing of the article as well as its contents.

The Saracens hooker, who was made England captain by Borthwick in 2024 before the role passed to Maro Itoje 12 months later, said that he did not recognise the situation described by the article.

"I can tell you that a lot of it's untrue," George told Rugby Union Weekly.

"We, as a squad, are incredibly disappointed by it.

"You just have to look at the timing of the article - two days out from our first Test match. I think it's clearly there to try and be divisive.

"It is the first time I think in my England career that as a group we've had to address an article that's been written, but we spoke about it brilliantly.

"Maro called a leader's meeting and thought that that was the best way of us going about it.

"Whoever's written this article, obviously their aim was for it to be divisive. Unfortunately for them, it's going to go the other way.

"This is going to galvanise us, it's going to make us tighter. We speak a lot about standing up for people, we speak a lot about helping each other, and we've got to make sure that we do that for Steve.

"He has had a bit of a personal attack here and an unwarranted one at that."

While none of the sources for the Times article were directly quoted in it, some of those previously involved in Borthwick's regime have criticised the set-up.

England's most-capped men's player Ben Youngs, who won the Premiership under Borthwick at Leicester and was part of his England squad at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, has described how he felt the head coach failed to offer sympathy and support when his family was affected by a terminal illness., external

Defence coach Felix Jones helped South Africa to back-to-back world titles, but lasted only seven months working under Borthwick before an "unstable working environment" reportedly motivated him to hand in his notice.

"The depiction is not something I recognise," Borthwick told Rugby Union Weekly of the Times article, emphasising that meetings between senior players and coaches are a feature of most coaching set-ups.

"As senior players part of our job is to challenge Steve," added George. "Steve is so open to us giving feedback and having challenge.

"It is very much a two-way conversation and that was definitely there in Argentina.

"There was an edge to what we were doing - there was plenty going on - but at no stage was it toxic.

"I don't know many organisations in the world that don't review big tournaments and try and make sure you take plenty of learnings."

England's autumn campaign begins against Australia on Sunday.

Borthwick will be acutely aware that it was at the same point in the World Cup cycle that his predecessor Eddie Jones was sacked.

The Australian, who, like Borthwick, had been heavily backed by the RFU, was eventually forced out after a November 2022 defeat by South Africa was met by a chorus of jeers from the Twickenham stands.

Allianz Stadium generates about 90% of the RFU's revenue, the vast majority of which comes via men's national team matchdays.

England's meeting with the Wallabies will be the first time Borthwick's team have returned to the venue since February's 42-21 loss to Ireland in a miserable Six Nations campaign.

While wins over Fiji and Argentina in their last two outings have ended a run of five straight losses, England's winning percentage for 2026 is still only 38%.

Only two years since the start of the Millennium have ended with a worse return.

After taking over from Jones, Borthwick very nearly led England to the Rugby World Cup final less than a year later, losing to South Africa by a single point in their semi-final.

His 2025 campaign fuelled hope with 11 wins from 12 matches, including a rare victory over New Zealand.

However, the momentum gathered on that run has evaporated.

The All Blacks, rejuvenated under new coach Dave Rennie, loom two weeks after Sunday's meeting with Australia, with a match against Japan, now led by Jones himself, in between.

Yonex serves up new partnership with Davis Cup
article_text:
Japanese sports equipment manufacturer Yonex has expanded its presence in international tennis after signing a multi-year partnership with the Davis Cup, becoming the official tennis ball partner of the Davis Cup by Generali Final 8.

Under the agreement, Yonex’s Tour Platinum tennis balls will be used as the official match balls for the 2026 edition, which will take place in Bologna, Italy, from November 24 to 29.

The partnership further strengthens Yonex’s association with international team tennis, following its appointment as the official ball supplier for the 2026 Billie Jean King Cup by Gainbridge Finals in Shenzhen, China. The latest agreement makes Yonex the official ball supplier for the finals of both men’s and women’s World Cup of Tennis competitions.

Beyond the two international team events, Yonex’s Tour Platinum is also being used across several leading ATP and WTA Tour tournaments, including the China Open in Beijing and the Rolex Shanghai Masters, extending the brand’s visibility across the professional tennis calendar.

Yonex President Alyssa Yoneyama said, “Representing their country is a special moment for any player, and we are honoured to support the athletes competing at the Davis Cup by Generali Final 8. Through Tour Platinum, we hope to give players that confidence to perform at their best as they represent their countries.”

World Tennis CEO Ross Hutchins added, “We are very excited that Yonex has joined our growing portfolio of premium partners for the Davis Cup by Generali. Yonex is one of the best tennis ball manufacturers in the game and is a fitting partner for the Final 8 – an incredible event that showcases the very best of our prestigious competition. We look forward to working with them in Bologna later this month.”

The agreement adds another specialist equipment partner to the Davis Cup’s expanding commercial portfolio. Generali was announced as the competition’s presenting partner in September, joining existing partners Rolex, Visa, MG, Fage, Corpay, Fred Perry and Betsson. Capital.com is also a partner of the Final 8.

The 2026 Final 8 will feature eight nations competing for the Davis Cup title, with three-time defending champions Italy joined by Czechia, Canada, South Korea, Great Britain, Germany, Austria and Spain.

title: Lidl boosts women’s cycling investment with La Vuelta Femenina presenting partnership
article_text:
Lidl is set to expand its presence in professional cycling after securing a multi-year partnership covering five of Spain’s leading cycling competitions from the 2027 season.

The agreement will see the German retail giant become the official fresh food partner across the events, further strengthening its association with the sport at both men’s and women’s levels.

The partnership encompasses La Vuelta, La Vuelta Femenina by Lidl, Itzulia Basque Country, Volta a Catalunya and Clásica San Sebastián. Lidl will also secure main partner status at La Vuelta, Itzulia Basque Country, Volta a Catalunya and Clásica San Sebastián, broadening its commercial presence across the Spanish cycling calendar.

A key element of the agreement is the retailer’s enhanced commitment to women’s cycling. Lidl will become the presenting partner of La Vuelta Femenina, with its name incorporated into the event’s official title. The company will also take on General Classification leader’s jersey sponsorship at both La Vuelta and La Vuelta Femenina, alongside leader’s jersey rights at Itzulia Basque Country.

Jens Thiemer, Chief Customer Officer Lidl Stiftung & Co. KG., said, “Cycling is part of everyday life and brings together many of the things Lidl stands for: conscious nutrition, an active lifestyle and genuine team spirit. That’s why our commitment deliberately goes beyond traditional brand visibility. We want to bring our strengths as a company to the table, working together with our partners to further develop cycling and inspire as many people as possible to get active.”

Javier Guillén, General Director of La Vuelta, added, “We are happy to begin this new partnership with Lidl, a company with a solid and proven track record of commitment to cycling. Its international reach and focus on balanced nutrition and active lifestyles make Lidl a natural partner for our events. We share the ambition to continue developing our events, enhancing the fan experience and bringing cycling closer to families and new audiences. We are also particularly pleased that this agreement will further strengthen Lidl’s support for La Vuelta Femenina and women’s cycling.”

Ruben Peris, Director of Volta a Catalunya, continued, “We are delighted to welcome Lidl as an Official Partner of La Volta a Catalunya from 2027. Lidl is a brand that is part of people’s everyday lives, and its commitment to La Volta is a great addition to our partner family. This partnership reinforces the connection between cycling and everyday life, while supporting one of the oldest and most historic stage races on the international cycling calendar.”

Javier Riaño, President of OCETA, shared, “We are delighted to welcome Lidl as a Main Partner of Itzulia Basque Country and Clásica San Sebastián from 2027. Having the support of a company with such a strong international presence and a proven commitment to cycling represents an important step forward for both races. This partnership goes beyond brand visibility, bringing together our shared values of promoting active lifestyles, balanced nutrition and a passion for cycling. We are confident that working alongside Lidl will help us continue developing our events, enhancing the experience for fans and bringing cycling closer to new audiences. We look forward to building a strong and successful long-term partnership.”

Beyond sponsorship visibility, the collaboration will include fan engagement initiatives, community activities and campaigns promoting balanced nutrition and active lifestyles.

The agreement builds on Lidl’s existing investment in professional cycling through its partnership with the Lidl-Trek men’s and women’s teams. It also aligns with the retailer’s broader ‘Feed Your Passion’ platform, which connects its food retail business with sport, nutrition and healthy living.

Although the financial terms and exact duration remain undisclosed, the five-event agreement represents a significant expansion of Lidl’s sports marketing portfolio. By combining event partnerships, jersey sponsorship and presenting rights, the retailer is positioning itself across multiple levels of professional cycling while strengthening its association with the growth of the women’s game.

title: Texas Tech details escalating payments in Galaxy stadium naming-rights deal
article_text: Texas Tech’s 15-year contract with Galaxy Digital Holdings LP for naming rights to Galaxy Stadium begins with Tech “due to receive” $4M in sponsorship fees for 2026-27, according to Don Williams of the LUBBOCK AVALANCHE-JOURNAL. With 3% annual increases, the payments top $5M for 2034-35 and exceed $6M for 2040-41, the final year. The sponsorship fees for each contract year are “due in two equal installments, half on July 1 and the other half on Jan. 1.” The annual fee payments add up to $74,395,650. An opt-out clause in the agreement “gives Galaxy sole discretion to terminate the contract on June 30, 2036.” Galaxy has a “contractual guarantee that Tech will host at least six home games a year.” The sponsorship also gives Galaxy the “option to use up to $100,000 of each annual sponsorship fee” on Tech athletes’ NIL endeavors. Texas Tech released the contract details Thursday after a ruling by the state attorney general’s office (LUBBOCK AVALANCHE-JOURNAL, 11/6).

title: Ireland captain Dan Sheehan stood down after Argentina win
article_text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan faces a spell on the sidelines after failing a head injury assessment during Friday night's 42-12 win over Argentina.

The Leinster hooker was having a pretty good evening in Dublin. He scored a try, Ireland were flying, and everything looked rosy.

Sheehan was forced off after 35 minutes and failed his HIA. Rónan Kelleher came on, and the captain's night was over.

Ireland boss Andy Farrell was quick to offer some good news after the final whistle.

"So we'll see tomorrow. Dan came off with a HIA, but seems fine, certainly in the dressingroom."

That's encouraging, but the medical team will have the final say.

Sheehan must undergo further checks before he can return. His place against Fiji on November 14 is far from certain.

It would be a bitter blow for the hooker, who had already crossed the whitewash in the 25th minute.

Ireland had recovered from an early Argentina try and were starting to turn the screw.

Unfortunately, Sheehan's injury wasn't the only talking point from a rather eventful first half.

Referee Luke Pearce also found himself in the firing line, with several decisions leaving Argentina supporters scratching their heads.

It certainly wasn't a quiet Friday night in Dublin.

Sheehan was not the only player to give Farrell a headache.

Ireland finished the match with several players requiring medical attention.

- Dan Sheehan: Failed his HIA and did not return.

- Robert Baloucoune: Forced off with an injury concern.

- Sean Jansen: Suffered a blow to his knee.

- Josh van der Flier: Picked up an ankle problem.

- Mack Hansen: Played on despite an ankle concern.

According to The Irish Times, Farrell confirmed that the medical team would assess the players following the match.

The timing is far from ideal, with Ireland preparing to face Fiji before a huge showdown with South Africa.

Injuries aside, it was a pretty good night at the office for Andy Farrell and his Ireland side.

Hugo Keenan stole the show with a superb hat-trick, while Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Rónan Kelleher also got in on the act.

Keenan was the star of the show, earning plenty of praise in RUCK's Ireland player ratings against Argentina.

Six tries, 42 points and a winning start to the Nations Championship. Farrell could hardly complain about the result.

The injury list, however, is another matter.

With Fiji up next and the mighty Springboks waiting around the corner, Ireland will need all hands on deck.

And preferably out of the treatment room.

Who impressed you most during Ireland's 42-12 victory?

Was Hugo Keenan your standout performer, or did another player deserve the plaudits?

title: LIV Golf timeline: Every twist and turn since league's launch
article_text:
Get the latest news, reviews, analysis and opinion, plus unmissable deals and exclusive offers. Please check the box of every email you wish to receive.

After five seasons, and over $5 billion spent, LIV Golf is finished.

Previously bankrolled by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia (PIF), The PIF’s decision to cut its backing in April left the league battling for its life.

In an effort to fix that, LIV partnered with proposed new investors, BC Partners Credit, in a bid to roll out a new era of the breakaway league dubbed LIV 2.0.

As part of this, the circuit filed for bankruptcy protection in October, and from there attempted to drum up support from players in a bid to ensure LIV could live on into 2027 and beyond.

On November 5, though, LIV’s fate was sealed. The circuit’s legal team claimed a restructuring would not take place, and instead the company would be winding down.

It was quite the underwhelming end after years of eye-watering signing fees, lucrative prize purses and head-to-head battles with rival tours.

January 2020 – The format for a rival golf league is proposed, as players and agents meet to discuss an 18-event circuit with just 48 players, 12 teams, no cut, a shotgun start and huge purses. It’s dubbed the ‘Premier Golf League’.

March 2020 – PGA Tour signs $700 million media rights deal, with PGL lurking. Comes shortly after Rory McIlroy raised concerns, “the more I’ve thought about it, the more I don’t like it.”

November 2020 – DP World Tour CEO Keith Pelley turns down the PGL and announces a strategic alliance that will see the PGA Tour take an ownership stake in European Tour productions.

April 2021 – PGA Tour launches ‘Player Impact Program’ (PIP) to reward players who bring the most value to the tour with bonuses.

May 2021 – According to reports, the ‘Super Golf League’ emerges, with Dustin Johnson and Phil Mickelson among those linked to it. Justin Rose also reportedly received an offer. It later became known as LIV Golf.

October 2021 – LIV Golf Investments names Greg Norman as its CEO. It commits $200 million to the Asian Tour (becoming $300 million in February 2022) and establishes a new elevated series of events called the International Series. The Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF) is named the majority shareholder in LIV Golf Investments.

November 2021 – PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan sends a memo to players, outlining massive purse increases for 2022.

February 2022 – Whilst playing in the Saudi International, Phil Mickelson slams the PGA Tour in a Golf Digest interview. He says its “obnoxious greed has really opened the door for opportunities elsewhere.”

Writer Alan Shipnuck later releases an excerpt from his upcoming biography of Mickelson, in which ‘Lefty’ says that despite their poor human rights record, “the Saudi money has finally given us that leverage [over the PGA Tour].”

Dustin Johnson and Bryson DeChambeau come out in support of the PGA Tour before Mickelson apologises on Twitter, announcing he will be taking time away from the game. Monahan then tells players that they won’t be able to compete on the PGA Tour if they jump ship.

March 2022 – Monahan addresses the media at the PLAYERS Championship and states the PGA Tour is “moving on” from the conversation surrounding other potential tours and that “we always will be focused on legacy, not leverage.”

Despite the setbacks, LIV Golf Investments announces a standalone eight-event, $255 million invitational series for 2022.

June 2022 – Several big names join as LIV stages first event at the Centurion Club near London. South Africa’s Charl Schwartzel wins by one stroke from compatriot Hennie Du Plessis.

July 2022 – Submits an application for inclusion on the Official World Golf Ranking. The OWGR says examination of which “will now commence.”

August 2022 – 11 LIV golfers file an antitrust lawsuit against the PGA Tour, alleging unlawful monopoly and restraint of trade.

Monahan announces huge changes to the Tour’s schedule and structure, including dramatic purse and bonus increases through a new series of “designated events”.

October 2022 – Announces a strategic alliance with the MENA Tour in a bid to gain immediate world ranking points, a subsequently unsuccessful move.

November 2022 – McIlroy insists it’s time for the bitter rivals to figure out their feud, but only if Norman leaves his position. “Greg needs to go. He needs to exit stage left,” McIlroy said. Woods soon agrees.

January 2023 – Announces long-awaited TV partner, CW Network, and schedule for 2023.

April 2023 – DP World Tour wins an arbitration case against LIV Golf players who were seeking to play the former European Tour. Arbitration panel rules that the DP World Tour had the right to fine and suspend players for violating its membership regulations to compete in LIV events.

June 2023 – “Framework agreement” is announced between the Public Investment Fund, the PGA Tour, and the DP World Tour to end all litigation and form a new entity. Said to be a ‘merger’, the plan is to finalise a deal by December 31.

August 2023 – DeChambeau shoots a final-round, 12-under 58 to win at Greenbrier. Remains the best round in LIV history.

October 2023 – OWGR rejects application for world ranking points. Norman later says he has “zero” concern for the future of the startup.

December 2023 – Jon Rahm turns back on the PGA Tour, claims lucrative deal was difficult to ignore, signing a contract estimated at more than $300 million.

title: Jamie George issues furious response to claim England have lost faith in Steve Borthwick
article_text:

The England hooker Jamie George has hit back at claims of a divided dressing room and toxic camp in a staunch defence of Steve Borthwick’s management ahead of their clash against Australia.

A report in The Times on Friday claimed that members of the England squad had lost faith in Borthwick during the first phase of the Nations Championship in July, and disagreed with the direction set by the head coach.

That followed the side’s worst-ever Six Nations campaign and first defeat to Italy earlier in the year, though George – who captained in the stead of the rested Maro Itoje in the summer – insisted that much of the reporting was wide of the mark.

“I don't relate to that in any way, shape, or form,” George said. “I'm incredibly disappointed by the article. I'm incredibly disappointed with the contents of it. I think there's a lot of it that's untrue. I'm incredibly disappointed with the timing. I think that holding it back two days out from a Test match is clearly trying to create a divide within the group.

“I am just incredibly upset by it if I am being honest. I don’t like the narrative it has created and the response from the group has been a rallying one because we all feel the same way. There are some people that are really angry about this article because it feels like an attack on Steve.

“It is just unwarranted. We had a meeting this morning and two days out from a Test match we are having to have a meeting about an article that’s been written about our head coach. I think that’s just crazy if I am honest, but we had to do it. We had to address it. The overriding thing that came out of it was that Steve has every bit of our backing and we need to make sure that we keep looking after each other like we have done for a very long time.”

George, Itoje and a group of senior players are understood to have called the whole squad together on Friday morning to address the article, with George Ford also said to have been a prominent voice.

The hooker confirmed that he had been among a group of leaders to have met with Borthwick after the summer Tests – which featured wins over Fiji and Argentina following a defeat to South Africa – to address improving the environment, though suggested this was common practice after each campaign.

Emphatic that the head coach retained the backing of the entire squad, George made clear that they intend to put on a performance for Borthwick against the Wallabies on Sunday.

“It’s galvanising, 100 per cent,” he said. “We are tight already, which that article doesn’t suggest. We are incredibly tight already. But when someone comes at one of our own, we are going to fight to protect them.

“That is genuinely across the board. We have meetings weekly with [assistant coach] Kevin Sinfield, and a lot of time Kev’s messaging comes back to looking after people and standing up for teammates and people we respect. That is what I think will happen now moving forward. My opinion, having read the article, is that given the timing it is trying to be divisive. I don’t see a world where it does that to us.”

England resume their Nations Championship campaign against Australia on Sunday, and also take on Japan, New Zealand and an unconfirmed opponent on the inaugural finals weekend this November.

Responding to the report, Borthwick said: “I'm aware of the article, I'm aware of the contents, I'm aware of some of the things it said. I don't recognise that as an accurate description of the environment.”

title: Jay Monahan opens up on controversial pre-LIV 'feeder tour' decision
article_text:
Why hadn’t he stopped the Saudis before they got started?

The implication here was that the Saudis — before they’d launched LIV, and as they were exploring the specifics of a new supercharged team-based golf league — had reached out to Monahan, seeking partnership, and that Monahan had ignored their call, and thus golf’s great war began.

Now Monahan has finally offered his side of the story.

Speaking to Eamon Lynch as part of a new Golf Channel show, Eamon Lynch Has Questions, Monahan addressed this particular bit of second-guessing.

“A lot of your critics said at the time that a lot of this could have been avoided had you taken a call from the Saudis at the outset, which doesn’t seem like such a smart piece of advice now that they’ve cut and run from the sport,” Lynch asked. “But why didn’t you take that call at the start?”

Monahan challenged the very premise of the question — that he was approached in good faith at any point — and instead painted the picture of a covert recruiting operation.

“First of all, I’m not aware of the ‘call’ that was made to me,” he said. “I do think anytime you’re gonna be negotiating with someone, you want to understand what their intent is, you want to understand how sincere they are. And if someone’s going to be calling me, or if someone did call me, you have to recognize, depending on what time this ‘call’ happened, that they had been at our tournaments as a team with their lawyers, recruiting our players, meeting with agents, doing all the things that they felt that they needed to do in order to stand up their league.

“I think the most important thing here is that it was their belief that franchise-based team golf was a more successful long-term proposition for the game than golf the way it’s played on the PGA Tour. That that model that is so successful in stick-and-ball sports could immediately translate to men’s professional golf, and that ultimately would win. And they saw us — they were saying this to others — as a feeder tour.”

That last bit felt like the heart of his answer, and one of the most important pieces of the interview: the Tour, which has been the world’s premier golf league for essentially the entirety of its existence, had no interest in engaging with a new tour seeking to exist as its superior. The nuance of the situation is tough to capture in a single sentence — for instance, when LIV first formed, the Premier Golf League was still trying to go live, too, and yes, I know this all feels like ancient history — but it paints a clearer picture of Monahan’s perspective.

“So if you’re gonna meet, then I think a couple things have to happen,” he continued. “You either have to agree that you need to become [a feeder tour] or largely become that, or you need to look inside and say, ‘What we’ve created is the right model for our players, for our fans, and for everybody that we serve.’ And that’s what was guiding us during that timeframe.

“It was not a pleasant period,” Monahan concluded. “We were focusing on the things that we could control, knowing what it was that we thought they were trying to do.”

Elsewhere in the interview Monahan acknowledged he’d handle some things differently with the benefit of hindsight. He specifically cited the rollout of the Tour’s framework agreement with LIV, which he called his “biggest regret.” As for the fact that the PGA Tour endures, while LIV is winding down? Monahan declined the opportunity to take a victory lap.

“I’m extremely proud of where we are and I’m extremely grateful to everyone that contributed to getting us here,” he said. “It’s not about me. You know, I was the leader of the organization during a challenging time. I did the best I could alongside everybody else to get us to the right outcome.”

Based on a quick browse of the interview I’m not sure there’s a place to watch the entire wide-ranging interview — but it will re-air at some point on Golf Channel and clips can be found here.

title: LALIGA and OSHEE expand their sponsorship agreement in Spain
article_text:
LALIGA and OSHEE have extended their sponsorship agreement in Spain through the 2027/2028 season, strengthening their strategic alliance. This milestone consolidates a global collaboration already active in 44 international markets, focused on sport, innovation, and the promotion of an active and healthy lifestyle through football.

The sponsorship agreement between LALIGA and OSHEE was officially signed at LEGENDS The Home of Football in Madrid, an iconic venue celebrating the history, trophies, and legacy of one of the world's most prestigious football leagues. The event was attended by official LALIGA ambassadors and Spanish football legends David Silva and Jesús Navas.

The partnership between LALIGA and OSHEE — one of Europe's leading brands in the functional drinks and hydration segment — now enters a new phase in Spain, a key strategic market for both organisations. The collaboration will continue to develop around the hydration category, including isotonic and electrolyte drinks. OSHEE, a brand originating from Poland, is positioning itself in Spain as a truly global brand, deeply rooted in sport and a performance-oriented lifestyle culture.

Since its beginnings, OSHEE has built its identity through close ties with elite sport, partnering with some of the most recognised organisations and figures in football and world athletics, including Real Madrid, Borussia Dortmund, and the Polish Football Federation. The brand has also worked with internationally renowned ambassadors such as Iga Świątek and Robert Lewandowski, reinforcing its strong connection with high performance, discipline, and sporting excellence.

The partnership with LALIGA, first launched in 2023 in Poland and subsequently expanded across Europe, now reaches a new milestone with its direct activation in Spain — home to one of the most competitive and widely followed football leagues in the world.

It is worth noting that numerous high-profile Polish players have featured in LALIGA, contributing to their clubs' success. They have played a part in securing victories and titles for their teams, yet never before in LALIGA's history had a Polish company been directly involved as a sponsor.

Jorge de la Vega, LALIGA's Director General of Business, stated: "The extension of our agreement with OSHEE in Spain represents a very significant step within a partnership that already has a strong international dimension. We share a common vision of how to connect with fans through sport, innovation, and unique experiences that deepen the emotional bond with LALIGA. We are very pleased to continue growing alongside a brand with a clear international ambition and a firm commitment to sport."

For his part, Jacek Łowigus, CEO of OSHEE Iberia, noted: "Spain represents a natural step in OSHEE's international growth. As a brand born in Poland but developed with global ambition, we have always been tied to sport and an active lifestyle. Our goal is to offer high-quality hydration solutions for everyone — from professional athletes to people who embrace an active daily life. Our partnership with LALIGA gives us a unique opportunity to bring this philosophy to one of the most passionate football markets in the world."

Through this agreement, OSHEE will develop various activations and campaigns alongside LALIGA aimed at fans, both in physical and digital environments, with the goal of continuing to drive visibility for both brands and promoting values associated with sport, hydration, and wellbeing.

OSHEE products will also be distributed through more than 40 commercial partners across Spain. In parallel, the brand is launching a new product portfolio designed specifically for Spanish consumers, comprising functional drinks enriched with electrolytes, minerals, and vitamins in six flavour varieties. Alongside these drinks, OSHEE is also introducing its range of protein bars to the market. Combining great taste with high nutritional value, these bars are designed to support an active lifestyle.

With this partnership, LALIGA continues to advance its global growth strategy alongside leading brands capable of connecting with fans and creating new experiences around football and entertainment.

title: Bombay Sapphire Named as Title Partner of the E1 Miami GP 2026 as Championship Returns to Miami
article_text:

Following a successful second season of global collaboration across iconic waterfront destinations, from Lake Como to Ibiza, Bombay Sapphire will now take a leading role in the E1 Championship's highly anticipated season finale in Miami.

Taking place on November 13 and 14, the race double-header will see the world's first electric raceboat Championship conclude its 2026 season, with Bombay Sapphire helping to bring together sport, culture and hospitality on Miami's waterfront.

As the E1 Miami GP Title Partner, Bombay Sapphire is now proudly sitting alongside the official event title and logo, in addition to debuting new co-branding on key E1 event and digital collateral – both within close proximity to the racing itself, as well as more widely around the city.

Bombay Sapphire will activate with E1 in and around Miami in the run-up to the event and over race days. Taste the Bombay Sapphire Sparkling Lemon, the official cocktail of E1, at participating Miami destinations across the city.

For the second consecutive year, Biscayne Bay will host the Championship’s electric fleet of E1 RaceBirds, featuring teams backed by star owners such as Tom Brady, LeBron James, Steve Aoki, and Marc Anthony.

Through its partnership with E1, Bombay Sapphire supports the Championship's wider focus on aquatic ecosystems, including as Presenting Partner of the E1 Blue Impact Championship, an initiative that encourages participating racing teams to contribute to aquatic conservation and restoration efforts.

Jamie Copas, Chief Executive Officer, E1 said: “We’re delighted that our long-term partnership with Bombay Sapphire continues to grow and for them to now become title partner for the Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami GP 2026 race double-header.

"We look forward to working with Bombay Sapphire to bring the partnership to life in Miami as we gear up for a landmark event, with the Championship’s first-ever double-header set to bring the 2026 season to a thrilling close."

Tara King, Senior Director, North America, Bombay Sapphire, said: “Bombay Sapphire’s ‘Step Into The Blue’ is our invitation to immerse in the beauty of life, and E1 is the ultimate expression of that. This is a fresh addition to the global sports category, bringing all-electric raceboat competition to waterfront cities around the world and drawing attention to the waters that make the sport possible. We brought ‘Step Into The Blue’ to life on the waterfront during E1’s North American debut last year, and we’re excited to build on what we started together.

“As Title Partner in Miami, we’re bringing that same spirit of discovery beyond the water and into the city – with the Bombay Sapphire Sparkling Lemon as the championship’s official cocktail, we’re giving new audiences an approachable way to discover gin and join the race weekend celebrations across Miami.”

title: Springboks star stood down moments before kick-off
article_text:
The Springboks have suffered a late setback ahead of their clash with Italy, with one of their starters withdrawn from the squad on matchday.

Rassie Erasmus is renowned for his unconventional team selections and psychological tactics, often abandoning the traditional Thursday announcement in favour of revealing his matchday 23 at unusual times.

The Springboks have also made late changes in the past due to injuries, although some have questioned whether certain withdrawals were part of Erasmus' mind games.

However, lock Salmaan Moerat has now been confirmed as unavailable, with Lood de Jager promoted to the starting second row and Franco Mostert moving onto the bench.

The change was announced on the Springboks' official X account shortly before kick-off, as the team confirmed the match was getting underway.

Moerat has endured several significant injury setbacks in recent seasons but had worked his way back into the international picture.

The 28-year-old's latest setback is particularly unfortunate, having only recently joined French side La Rochelle from the Stormers.

Moerat previously captained the Stormers, becoming their first skipper in the United Rugby Championship when the competition launched in 2021.

Erasmus had initially surrounded Moerat with plenty of experience for the Italy encounter, giving the lock an opportunity to establish himself alongside some of South Africa's most trusted forwards.

His withdrawal means he misses the chance to answer questions over his selection, with doubts raised about whether he could deliver the physical presence expected of a Springbok starting lock.

His father, Nazeem Moerat, played for the non-racial SARU team during the apartheid era, and multiple uncles and cousins have played top-tier rugby.

He has worn the captain's armband at almost every tier of his career. Moerat captained his school (Paarl Boys' High), the Western Province U18s during the iconic Craven Week, and the Junior Springboks (South Africa U20). He was also chosen as the DHL Stormers' first captain in the United Rugby Championship (URC) back in 2021.

After spending nine years coming through the ranks in Cape Town, he made a high-profile international move to France, joining La Rochelle.

Moerat stands at an imposing 2.00 metres (6 feet 7 inches) tall and weighs between 116 kg and 122 kg.

title: "Illegal tactics" – Steve Borthwick lodged official complaint about Australia
article_text:
England head coach Steve Borthwick sparked a furious row with Australia in 2025 after raising concerns over the Wallabies' alleged illegal breakdown tactics with match officials.

The England boss reportedly identified dozens of questionable clearouts ahead of their meeting at Twickenham, with player safety at the heart of his concerns.

Captain Harry Wilson accused England of whinging, while then-head coach Joe Schmidt dismissed the controversy as gamesmanship.

Now, with England and Australia preparing to renew their rivalry at Twickenham on Sunday in the Nations Championship, the controversy has resurfaced.

And if last year's war of words is anything to go by, there could be plenty of fireworks when the two sides meet again.

According to The Telegraph, Borthwick met referee Nika Amashukeli before the November 2025 encounter.

England had reportedly identified around 40 potential illegal entries at the breakdown during Australia's previous matches against the British & Irish Lions, South Africa, New Zealand and Argentina.

Approximately 20 were considered clear-cut infringements.

The concern centred on Australian players entering rucks from the side rather than through the legal entry point.

Such clearouts can put opposition players at risk, particularly those attempting to steal possession.

Under World Rugby's laws, arriving players must join a ruck from behind their offside line.

England believed Australia had repeatedly pushed those boundaries without being punished.

Wallabies captain Harry Wilson was having none of it.

The back-row forward rejected suggestions that Australia deliberately used illegal or dangerous tactics.

"Firstly, I'd like to question how many of them are illegal."

He also defended Schmidt, insisting the Australian coach would never deliberately encourage his players to break the laws.

Wilson pointed out that Australia had contested more than 2,000 rucks that year, suggesting England had selected a handful of incidents to make their case.

The captain also accused England of whinging about the breakdown.

It was hardly the friendliest build-up to a Test match.

England eventually won the November 2025 encounter 25-7, but the argument did not end with the final whistle.

Schmidt accused England of gamesmanship and questioned the figures reported before the match.

According to The Independent, the Australian coach insisted that only ten incidents had been submitted to Amashukeli.

He also claimed the referee did not agree that every example was illegal.

Schmidt defended Australia's disciplinary record, pointing out that his side had completed more than 1,200 attacking rucks that year without any player being forced off injured by their clearouts.

The New Zealander insisted the controversy had not distracted his players or influenced the referee.

Borthwick, meanwhile, praised Amashukeli's performance but acknowledged England still had work to do at the breakdown.

title: Elena Rybakina's WTA Finals participation in doubt after latest health issue
WTA apologises to Pegula for broadcast of ‘diva’ comment about Andreeva
article_text:
Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) chief Valerie Camillo apologised after a courtside microphone captured United States star Jessica Pegula making disparaging comments about rival Mirra Andreeva.

Pegula was plunged into controversy after her conversation with coach Mark Knowles on a practice court at Indian Wells in California was broadcast on a WTA YouTube livestream of the session.

In the exchange, Pegula can be heard describing 19-year-old Russian Andreeva as a “diva”.

World number four Pegula was also heard criticising Andreeva’s coach, former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez, for not addressing French Open champion Andreeva’s behaviour.

Speaking before Sunday’s opening matches of the WTA Finals, WTA chairperson Camillo blamed the controversy on “several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream given our own policies and procedures”.

“I want to apologise on behalf of the entire WTA for these occurrences,” Camillo said at a news conference on Friday.

“The WTA is sensitive to player privacy and has policies and procedures in place to balance players’ needs for safe spaces with opportunities to bring fans closer to the game.

“There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area,” she added, confirming that all audio recording equipment in practice areas had since been removed.

Camillo said microphones had been installed on practice courts to pick up “ambient sound” – such as the noise of balls being struck – rather than conversations between players and coaches.

“So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution and monitoring,” Camillo said, before directly apologising to Pegula and Knowles.

“I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and Mark Knowles,” she added.

“What happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA’s best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction.”

The WTA Finals begin on Sunday, with the top eight women’s singles players divided into two round-robin groups of four before advancing to the knockout rounds.

title: Ahn Se-young extends dominance with 53-match win streak in Korea Open
article_text:
'shuttlecock queen' Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance)'s overwhelming performance even drew praise from Taiwanese media. Ahn Se-young defeated Japan's KUNJI Riko (world ranking 20) in 37 minutes to continue her bid for a season-high 11th title.

Taiwan's Liberty Times on the 6th (Korean time) reported the news of Ahn Se-young's advance to the Korea Open semifinals under the headline "Who can beat her? The invincible Ahn Se-young completely dominated a Japanese powerhouse. This year's record is a historic 69 wins and 1 loss."

The outlet praised, "Korea's invincible queen Ahn Se-young defended her home. Ahn Se-young comfortably advanced to the semifinals at the Super 500 Korea Open held today, defeating Japan's powerhouse KUNJI Riko 21-7, 21-13."

World No. 1 Ahn Se-young in the women's singles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do, defeated KUNJI by a game score of 2-0 (21-7, 21-13).

It was literally an overwhelming performance. Ahn Se-young briefly struggled against KUNJI's sharp attacks early in the first game but quickly turned the momentum. With precise attacks that targeted every corner of the court and flawless defense, she pressed her opponent and reached the interval at 11-7.

After that, she did not concede a single point to KUNJI. Ahn Se-young scored 11 consecutive points starting from 10-7 to take the first game 21-7. KUNJI was helpless, unable to break through Ahn Se-young's defense.

Liberty Times also noted this scene. The outlet explained, "Ahn Se-young unleashed her attacking power from the first game. Leading 10-7, she mounted an incredible surge of 11 consecutive points to take the first game."

The second game was no different. Ahn Se-young did not waver despite KUNJI's persistent chase. She anticipated her opponent's attacks and built points with sharp counterattacks. In the end, Ahn Se-young closed out the match in just 37 minutes by taking the second game 21-13, and KUNJI had to feel the high wall of the world No. 1.

Even in Japan they acknowledged the complete defeat. Japanese badminton specialist outlet Badminton Spirit, covering KUNJI's loss, assessed, "KUNJI failed to show her strengths against queen Ahn Se-young and lost 0-2." KUNJI has shown good form recently, but she could not properly exert her strength against Ahn Se-young.

Global badminton specialist media Badminton Planet also spotlighted Ahn Se-young's near-perfect performance. The outlet reported, "Ahn Se-young once again showed overwhelming form against Japan's KUNJI Riko in front of home fans."

It went on to explain that Ahn Se-young scored 11 consecutive points from 10-7 in the first game and maintained control in the second game to secure her place in the semifinals. It particularly highlighted the remarkable record of 53 consecutive wins and a season mark of 69 wins and 1 loss.

In fact, Ahn Se-young's record this season is nearly unbelievable. With this victory she recorded 69 wins and 1 loss in 70 international matches, a winning percentage of 98.57%. Since losing to Wang Zhiyi (China) in the All England Open final last March, she has won an astonishing 53 consecutive matches.

Liberty Times emphasized, "With this win Ahn Se-young raised her season record to an almost unbelievable 69 wins and 1 loss. Her only defeat came in the All England Open final last March against China's Wang Zhiyi."

Ahn Se-young this year has topped 10 tournaments: the Malaysia Open, the India Open, the Asian Championships, the Singapore Open, the Indonesia Open, the world championships, the China Masters, the Asian Games, the Denmark Open and the French Open. If she also wins the Korea Open, she would surpass last year's record as the first women's singles player to win 11 titles in a single season and become the first player since the launch of the BWF World Tour to achieve 11 or more wins in two consecutive seasons.

Liberty Times added, "Ahn Se-young continues to dominate the women's singles stage. Having already claimed 10 trophy wins this season, she is gunning for her 11th title this week."

Ahn Se-young's next opponent is also Japanese. She will face world No. 16 Akechi Hina in the women's singles semifinal on the 7th. Akechi advanced by defeating world No. 7 Miyazaki Tomoka 2-1 (13-21, 23-21, 21-8) in the quarterfinals. On the opposite side of the draw, world No. 2 Yamaguchi Akane (Japan) and Lin Xiang-ti (Taiwan) will compete for a place in the final.

title: World No. 1 Seo-Kim Pair Stage Comeback Victory After Seven Months
article_text:
Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho defeated the Chinese pair Wang Chang-Xi Haonan 2-1 (21-14, 15-21, 21-19) in the men's doubles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held on November 6 at the Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium.

[OSEN=Yeosu, Ko Seong-hwan Reporter] The 'world No. 1' Seo Seung-jae-Kim Won-ho pair (Samsung Life Insurance) achieved a dramatic comeback victory through their relentless determination. The two players, who barely advanced to the semifinals, vowed in front of Korean fans to secure their first victory in about seven months.

Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho defeated the Chinese pair Wang Chang-Xi Haonan 2-1 (21-14, 15-21, 21-19) in the men's doubles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held on November 6 at the Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium.

It was a tough battle. The Seo-Kim pair won the first game 21-14 with stable defense and exquisite attacks. However, they lost the second game 15-21, overwhelmed by the Chinese pair's strong counterattack.

The third game also brought a crisis. The Seo-Kim pair started strong at 3-0 but allowed the opponents to score five consecutive points, losing momentum. With unforced errors piling up, the score gap widened to 11-16.

However, the world No. 1's prowess was formidable. The Seo-Kim pair scored five straight points to tie at 16-16 and surged ahead to reach match point first at 20-18.

The longest rally of the day, which decided the match, was the highlight. Seo Seung-jae barely received the shuttlecock even after falling on the court. He got back up to continue his defense and finally scored the decisive point, putting an end to the intense battle.

In the mixed zone after the match, Seo Seung-jae reflected, "I think that movement came from trying to receive the shuttle no matter what. Even though I fell, I quickly got up thinking that if I could somehow return one more shot, Kim Won-ho would cover for me."

It was a nerve-wracking moment for Kim Won-ho, who was watching from behind. He smiled and said, "There were many tense moments throughout. Especially in the final moments, my racket broke. I was relieved that Seung-jae defended and finished the point."

The driving force behind their three-game comeback victory was their trust in each other. Seo Seung-jae stated, "Even though we were trailing, I thought good chances would come if we kept playing well until the end. Today, we challenged ourselves with the mindset of not giving up until the end and following each point."

Partner Kim Won-ho also emphasized, "We could have collapsed during the third game. However, we maintained trust in Seung-jae until the end and kept fighting without giving up. The fans' enthusiastic support also gave us more strength."

Another driving force repeatedly emphasized by the two players was the passionate support from home fans. The spectators at Jinnam Gymnasium that day did not hesitate to encourage the pair even in moments when the match seemed to be slipping away.

Kim Won-ho said, "Since this is a tournament held in Korea, I think the good results were possible thanks to the support from many spectators. I consider it an honor," crediting the fans. Seo Seung-jae also conveyed, "Although there were many difficulties, we were able to come back and win thanks to the support from many fans. I would like to express my gratitude."

Now, the Seo-Kim pair are challenging for their second consecutive Korea Open title and a victory after about seven months. Since reuniting in early 2025, they have won an impressive 11 tournaments. However, this year, after winning the Malaysia Open in January, the All England Open in March, and the Asian Championships in April, they failed to reach the top in nine consecutive tournaments.

Seo Seung-jae emphasized, "If we win in Korea, I think we can use it as a springboard to play even better. I really want to win this time." Kim Won-ho also pledged, "Last year, we won many unexpected titles, so we end up making comparisons. I think we are doing well enough even now. Above all, I am grateful to be injury-free. Since this is the last tournament held in Korea, I will do my best to win."

title: Adam Scott sends clear message to LIV Golf stars after league's closure
PGA Tour players deliver brutal verdict on LIV Golf stars' potential return: 'Go back to Q-School'
article_text:
Former LIV Golf stars could face a seriously uncomfortable route back to the PGA Tour, with current members making it clear that a return to the circuit should come at a price.

Erik van Rooyen delivered perhaps the most brutal response when Golfweek asked players about the future of LIV Golf's biggest names at the WWT Championship in Mexico.

With LIV Golf now dead, attention has turned to where its biggest names go next.

Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia and Bryson DeChambeau all have a route to the DP World Tour in 2027, while Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Joaquin Niemann are likely to rely on tournament invitations.

But a return to the PGA Tour is a much more complicated proposition.

While the return of golf's biggest names would undoubtedly boost the PGA Tour, not everyone is prepared to welcome them back with open arms.

Van Rooyen believes those who walked away should have to fight their way back into the system.

“We were told initially that if you played LIV, you would be banned from the PGA Tour, and the story just kept changing,” the South African told Golfweek.

“They gave the finger to the Tour. If you're that good, go get it done.”

The 2023 WWT Championship winner also questioned why former LIV players should retain privileges that others have spent years working to secure.

“I have nothing against those players, but if I went home and played the Sunshine Tour for three or four years, I'm not being welcomed back with my old spot on the PGA Tour,” he added.

Former Masters champion Adam Scott appears to share that sentiment, insisting that returning players should have to prove themselves again.

“I think the fairest thing is that they all re-establish themselves in the system that they want to go to,” Scott told Today's Golfer.

“They left and gave up those privileges. So, you know, I think they should re-qualify themselves.”

Not every player is demanding the same punishment.

Lucas Glover acknowledged the devastating impact LIV Golf's collapse could have on employees, but believes the players who defected should still face consequences.

“A lot of people lost their jobs, people with families and bills to pay, so, from a human being standpoint, it sucks,” Glover said.

However, he added: “I do think penalties need to be served.”

Glover would nevertheless welcome the return of stars such as Rahm and DeChambeau, provided they satisfy the PGA Tour's requirements.

“If they meet the criteria to come back, sure,” he said. “It makes the Tour more appealing.”

Camilo Villegas, a member of the Tour's Policy Board, was more guarded, refusing to reveal his position ahead of an upcoming board meeting.

Peter Malnati, meanwhile, believes LIV Golf's downfall was inevitable.

“It didn't take too much to see that that wasn't a viable economic model,” he said.

Malnati, who is in contention at the WWT Championship, also suggested the PGA Tour had emerged stronger from the battle, despite the disruption caused by LIV Golf's arrival.

LIV Golf's demise leaves many of its leading players searching for their next destination.

Several, including Rahm, Hatton and Garcia, retain full DP World Tour status, while others such as Niemann and Johnson will be reliant on invites.

The PGA Tour is a different matter, with returning players facing suspension periods and eligibility hurdles.

Garcia made clear to GolfMagic this week that he would be interested in a return, despite his acrimonious departure in 2022.

Whether the PGA Tour chooses to welcome its former rebels back, impose penalties or demand a fresh qualifying campaign remains to be seen.

One thing is clear: the red carpet is not being rolled out for everyone.

And if van Rooyen gets his way, the biggest names in LIV Golf will have to start from scratch.

title: Russia’s rocky return to global sport
‘It’s almost like a nightclub’: Hyrox takes off in China amid fitness frenzy
Slick Saints beat Prem Rugby Cup holders Leicester
article_text:
Northampton kept their hopes of reaching the Prem Rugby Cup semi-finals alive after a dominant 39-19 derby victory over East Midlands rivals Leicester.

A youthful Saints line-up turned on the style to sink the holders at Franklin's Gardens and stretch Northampton's run to 16 successive home wins in all competitions.

Wings Tom Rowe and Amena Caqusau and full-back James Martin all touched down twice in a seven-try romp for the Saints.

After three successive defeats in the Prem Rugby Cup, last season's winners Leicester are bottom of Pool B.

It was not a perfect evening for Northampton. Already without two injured scrum-halves in England international Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland, the Saints lost a third in the 29th minute in Jonny Weimann.

The 20-year-old, made captain for the evening, limped off after creating Northampton's first two tries, number one in the 11th minute with a glorious long pass to Martin and number two five minutes later with a cross-kick to Rowe.

But England Under-18s scrum-half Sonny Goode showed Northampton's remarkable depth in the position with an impressive showing off the bench.

After being steamrollered in a feisty Prem meeting at Mattioli Woods Welford Road a fortnight ago, this emphatic win provided a measure of revenge.

Saints led 27-7 at the break with Rowe, Caqusau and centre Toby Thame also crossing.

Caqusau produced a fine finish to secure the bonus point for Saints in the 36th minute and Rowe's second on the stroke of half-time gave Saints their 20-point interval advantage.

But Martin went over for his second from a cross-kick in the 46th minute and then Caqusau added his second after some fine approach play by Goode with Leicester wing Adam Radwan in the sin-bin.

Leicester, well beaten, managed three tries, two from hooker Sam Moli and one from back row Osian Thomas.

Sale Sharks went to the top of Pool A with a tense 21-19 win over Bristol Bears at the CorpAcq Stadium.

Two tries from Arron Reed - playing at full-back - and one from Alex Wills did the damage but Bristol took the game to the wire with two tries from Max Pepper after Totoa Auvaa, the Samoan hooker given a second chance by director of rugby Pat Lam following his sacking by Saracens for his off-field conduct, had opened their account.

title: WTA chair apologises to Pegula for airing of 'diva' comment
article_text:
Women's Tennis Association chair Valerie Camillo has apologised to Jessica Pegula and said the live-streaming of private comments to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva was "regrettable and unacceptable".

American Pegula called Andreeva a "diva" in a private conversation with her coach after a practice session for the WTA Tour Finals on Wednesday.

However, the comments were aired on a live stream after the WTA failed to tell players there were microphones on practice courts.

World number five Pegula called the incident "unfortunate" and said the WTA players' council supported players' calls for more privacy.

Camillo said that all audio recording equipment in practice areas had since been removed as "clearly there was a failure in our technical execution and monitoring".

"I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles," she added.

"What happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction."

Pegula was also heard saying French Open champion Andreeva "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour.

A representative for Pegula said she had been in direct contact with those involved and had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones.

None of the players were asked about the incident in the pre-tournament news conference at Indian Wells on Friday, but Pegula did address it in an interview with ESPN.

"I think it's something that we have fought a lot over the last couple years as there's a lot more surveillance and audio and access to the players at tournaments than there has been in the past," she said., external

"I know for broadcasting that it's great for fans, but I think we've seen a couple incidents now throughout the year, [the] last couple of years really, where it just seems highly unnecessary.

"I think [this will] definitely reignite the topic and, hopefully, we can unfortunately use this incident to keep pushing for more player privacy."

Pegula's compatriot Coco Gauff called for more privacy after she was captured in the players' area smashing a racquet following a defeat by Elina Svitolina in the Australian Open quarter-finals in January.

At the same major, six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek said players were being watched "like animals in the zoo" by behind-the-scenes cameras.

YouTube streams of Wednesday's practice sessions at Indian Wells have since been removed by the WTA, but the footage had already been shared on social media.

Referring to the incident in California, where the season-ending WTA Finals are being held, Camillo added: "The WTA is sensitive to player privacy and has policies and procedures in place to balance players' needs for safe spaces with opportunities to bring fans closer to the game.

"There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area."

title: 1X Bet Cup: Ighalo urges more corporate bodies to embrace sports sponsorship
